passage:
Pooja: the product page has to go live on the 30th. i'm panicking 😰
Swati: ok. what has to be true on the 29th?
Pooja: um. final approval from Rohan's team
Swati: and for that to happen on the 29th?
Pooja: pictures shot, text checked. so the 25th
Swati: shooting needs the samples. have you ordered them?
Pooja: not yet. the supplier needs a week to send them
Swati: and today is the 14th. so?
Pooja: so i have to order the samples today and book the photographer. wait. that means we are already late 😳
Swati: you're not. you just found the real start date. want to book the photographer now?
Pooja: yes. calling right now

qa.q: On which date does the product page have to go live?
qa.a: The product page has to go live on the 30th.

qa.q: How does Pooja feel when the backward steps show the real start date?
qa.a: Pooja is first alarmed, saying “we are already late”, and worried, though Swati's steady reply helps turn that into a plan.

qa.q: What did working backwards from the 30th reveal?
qa.a: It revealed that the samples must be ordered and a photographer booked today, and that the work depends on other people such as the supplier and the photographer.

qa.q: What might Swati be thinking when asking “what has to be true” at each step?
qa.a: Swati is calm and patient, treating the deadline as a chain of earlier steps and asking questions so Pooja can see the chain without being handed the answer.

grounding: An experienced planner works backwards from the deadline and reveals the true start date and dependencies.

passage: Pema had one fixed date: the stall at the district fair opened on the twelfth. In her sister's tea shop, Pema sat with a pencil and asked the question again and again. What must be true on the eleventh? Banner hung and stock counted. On the ninth? Banner printed. The town press needed three days and a proof on paper, so the design had to be ready by the fifth. Asif at the press needed the photograph first, which was still with a relative in the next village. Pema counted the days on her fingers and laughed once. Today was the third. She put down the pencil and went to fetch the photograph herself, by bus, that afternoon.

qa.q: On which date did the stall at the district fair open?
qa.a: The stall at the district fair opened on the twelfth.

qa.q: Why did Pema laugh once when counting on her fingers?
qa.a: Pema realised the real start date was already here, since today was the third and the design was due on the fifth; it was a mix of surprise and dry amusement.

qa.q: What did Pema do first once she saw the dependencies?
qa.a: She went to fetch the photograph herself by bus that afternoon, because the press needed it before starting.

qa.q: How might Asif at the press see Pema's timing?
qa.a: Asif may feel some pressure because Pema's date depends on the press finishing in three days, but a clear deadline lets Asif plan the work early.

grounding: An experienced planner asks what must be true one step earlier, back to today, and finds the true start date and dependencies.

passage: The wedding was on 14 June in a village hall outside Porto, and Mateo was the one his sister had trusted to plan it. Sami, his flatmate, found him at the kitchen table with a calendar. "I'm starting at the end," Mateo said. "Fourteenth: wedding. What must be true on the thirteenth? Chairs set up, flowers delivered." He wrote it. "For flowers on the thirteenth, the florist needs the order by the first." Another line. "For the order, my sister must choose colours by late May." He kept going until he reached today, 20 April. His pen stopped. "The caterer needs a deposit this week. I thought I had a month." He picked up the phone.

qa.q: On what date was the wedding?
qa.a: The wedding was on 14 June.

qa.q: What was Mateo feeling when his pen stopped at today's date?
qa.a: He felt startled and a bit alarmed, discovering the caterer needed a deposit this week when he thought he had a month.

qa.q: Why does working backwards help Mateo more than starting from today?
qa.a: Asking what must be true one step earlier exposes each dependency, like the florist's order and his sister's colour choice, and shows the real start date.

qa.q: How might Mateo's sister be affected by his method?
qa.a: She will need to decide on colours sooner than expected, but she can trust that the wedding tasks will be ready on time.

grounding: Shows a planner working backwards from a fixed date to discover the true starting point and dependencies on others.

passage: In the school staffroom, Imran spread a chart across two desks. The annual sports day was on 10 December. Darshan, the new PE teacher, had planned to "start preparing in November". Imran shook his head. "Let's walk backwards. On the ninth, the field must be marked. For that, the lime powder must arrive by the fifth. For the lime, we need the principal's signature on the purchase form by late November." Darshan wrote fast. "Parents' permission slips? Those take ten days to come back." "Then they go out by the fifteenth." When they reached today's date, 28 October, Darshan laughed nervously. "So we start tomorrow." "We start today," said Imran.

qa.q: When was the annual sports day?
qa.a: The annual sports day was on 10 December.

qa.q: What does Darshan's nervous laugh suggest?
qa.a: It suggests Darshan felt anxious and caught out, realising the plan to start in November was already too late.

qa.q: What did Imran's method reveal that Darshan's plan missed?
qa.a: Working backwards revealed dependencies on the principal's signature, the lime supplier and parents returning slips, which pushed the real start to today.

qa.q: How might the principal see the purchase form arriving on time?
qa.a: The principal would probably feel relieved and see the PE department as organised, rather than being rushed at the last minute.

grounding: An experienced teacher works backwards from an event date to show the true starting date and dependencies on other people.

passage:
Dear Sonali,

You asked how I planned the community library opening without panicking. Here's the trick my old manager taught me: begin at the end.

The opening was 1 March. So on 28 February, the shelves had to be full. For that, the books had to be labelled by the 20th. For labelling, the volunteers had to be trained by the 10th, which meant sending the volunteer call-out by mid-January. And the donation drive, which fed everything, had to start before Christmas.

When I reached the day I was writing the plan, I gasped. I was already a week late! But at least I knew. I called the volunteers that afternoon.

Take care,
Nazia

qa.q: When was the community library opening?
qa.a: The opening was 1 March.

qa.q: How did Nazia feel on reaching the day the plan was being written?
qa.a: Nazia gasped, feeling shocked and a little alarmed to be already a week late, but also relieved to know it.

qa.q: What could Sonali copy from Nazia's method?
qa.a: Sonali could write the final date first and keep asking what must be ready one step earlier, noting which people each step depends on.

qa.q: How might the volunteers be affected by Nazia's backwards plan?
qa.a: They would get their call-out and training in time, instead of being rushed to label books days before the opening.

grounding: A planner's letter shows working backwards from a deadline to find the real start date and the people each step depends on.

passage:
Parveen, you asked how I moved my parents from Kanpur to Pune without a single disaster. I'm Reena, and I did it backwards.
The one fixed date was 1 June: the new flat's handover. So I asked, what has to be true on 31 May? The truck loaded, the old flat empty. For that, the movers had to be booked by the 15th, because in summer they're full. For the truck to take the furniture, Papa's cupboards had to be emptied by the 25th, and Papa takes a week to sort one drawer, so we started on the 10th.
Then the gas connection: cancelling takes ten days, so I applied on the 12th. The bank address change needs the new rent agreement, so the landlord had to send it by the 5th.
When I reached today, the plan said: start on 3 May. It was already 4 May. I phoned the landlord that afternoon.
Working backwards showed me the real start date, and all the people I was waiting on.

qa.q: What was the one fixed date?
qa.a: 1 June: the new flat's handover.

qa.q: How might Reena have felt when the plan said to start on 3 May?
qa.a: Reena probably felt a jolt of alarm, realising the real start date had already passed, and acted quickly.

qa.q: Why did working backwards help Reena more than starting from today?
qa.a: It showed the true start date and every dependency on other people, like the movers, the landlord and the gas office.

qa.q: How might Reena's father have felt about starting on his cupboards so early?
qa.a: Papa might have grumbled at first but been relieved not to rush, since he takes a week to sort one drawer.

grounding: Illustrates a planner who starts from the deadline and asks what must be true one step earlier, exposing the real start date and dependencies.
